fact: Git reads ~/.config/git/ignore (XDG default) as a global gitignore automatically — core.excludesFile does NOT need to be set
recommendation: Before suggesting `git config --global core.excludesFile <path>`, check whether ~/.config/git/ignore already exists. If it does, git is already using it — just append to that file. Setting core.excludesFile to a different path silently overrides the XDG file. Verify with `git check-ignore -v <path>` to see which gitignore source actually matches.

fact: lstat(path) permission requires SEARCH (X) on path's PARENT directory, NOT on path itself — chmod 0 on child/ does NOT block lstat(child). Source: POSIX path resolution + dirent lookup. To trigger 'readdir succeeds but lstat-on-entries fails' for tests: chmod 0o400 (R only) on the PARENT — readdir needs R, lstat needs X on parent.
recommendation: Tests asserting per-entry lstat failure under DAC must chmod the PARENT to remove X but keep R. chmod on the child target does nothing for lstat-via-parent's-dirent. Pair with `if (process.getuid?.() === 0) soft-skip` for environments that bypass DAC.

fact: vi.spyOn on `import * as ns from 'node:fs'` namespace throws `TypeError: Cannot redefine property: <name>` / `Module namespace is not configurable in ESM`. ESM namespace objects are frozen by spec; spyOn cannot rewrite their property descriptors. Affects any node:fs / node:path / node:os spy attempt under Vitest with ESM.
recommendation: Don't try `vi.spyOn(fsModule, 'lstatSync')` on ESM. Alternatives: (a) `vi.mock('node:fs', () => ({...actual, lstatSync: vi.fn(...)}))` at file scope (factory hoisted; affects all tests in file — isolate via dedicated test file); (b) refactor production import to `import * as fs from 'node:fs'` AND use `fs.lstatSync(...)` everywhere (live binding through namespace, but invasive); (c) use real syscalls via chmod + soft-skip-if-root + static-grep canary. Option (c) cleanest when behavior is OS-observable.

provenance.reference: web/scripts/detect-stack.test.ts:608 — initial A4 attempt failed with this exact error

fact: `existsSync(path)` swallows ALL errors including EACCES/EIO and returns false — the caller cannot distinguish 'file absent' from 'file present but unreadable'. Wrappers that do `if (!existsSync(p)) return absent; lstatSync(p)` therefore silently treat unreadable-but-present files as absent, never reaching the lstatSync catch path that would surface read_error. Was exactly the case in detect-stack.ts:resolveMarker — fine for per-marker probes that re-check, wrong for new enumeration callers wanting failure surfacing.
recommendation: To distinguish absent vs unreadable: skip existsSync; call lstatSync(path) directly in try/catch and inspect `err.code`. ENOENT → absent; EACCES/EIO/ELOOP → read_error. existsSync's blanket-false-on-error is correct ONLY for boolean 'do we attempt the next step' decisions, never for failure-mode reporting.

provenance.reference: web/scripts/detect-stack.ts enumerateCandidatePrefixes A4 surfacing — resolveMarker wrapper silently dropped EACCES via existsSync-first

fact: `Dirent.isDirectory()` from `readdirSync(dir, {withFileTypes:true})` is NOT a symlink gate. On filesystems whose readdir(3) returns DT_UNKNOWN (some network FS, FUSE, older ext layers), Node falls back to a stat-style probe that FOLLOWS symlinks — so a symlink-to-directory will report isDirectory() === true. `lstatSync(path).isSymbolicLink()` is the authoritative symlink check.
recommendation: Never rely on Dirent.isDirectory()/.isFile() as a security boundary for symlink rejection. Use lstatSync explicitly. Comments claiming '!entry.isDirectory() also rejects symlinks' are wrong and ship a silent EC-7-class boundary regression on DT_UNKNOWN filesystems.

fact: A fs-cleanup skip-set keyed on RAW paths silently fails to match entries the sweeper canonicalises via realpathSync — under any symlinked ancestor (macOS $TMPDIR→/private/var, container bind-mounts) the skip is defeated and live files get deleted.
recommendation: Canonicalise BOTH sides of a delete/skip comparison. If the consumer realpaths entries (resolveCleanupPath), the producer's active/exclusion set must realpath too. Open files always realpath-resolve; fall back to raw only on a close-race. Test with a symlinked-ancestor root driven through the REAL producer getter, not a hand-built raw Set (that test is tautological on Linux CI where raw==realpath).

fact: A content fingerprint recomputed on the reader side from /proc/<pid>/cmdline drops empty tokens (kernel cmdline ends in a trailing NUL → trailing empty segment), so a writer hashing the raw argv with empties produces a digest the reader can never match → false 'mismatch' and a leaked resource.
recommendation: When a hash is recomputed on the other side from an OS-canonicalised source (/proc cmdline, realpath, normalised JSON), apply the SAME canonicalisation in the producer. For argvSha256, filter empty tokens before NUL-joining: args.filter(s=>s.length>0).join(String.fromCharCode(0)). Pin with a test asserting an empty token in any position is a hashing no-op.

fact: During a normal Codex model-switch relaunch, both session_phase:terminated AND cli_disconnected fire transiently before the new session_init lands.
recommendation: Do NOT clear in-flight switch/UI state (pendingCodexModelSwitch) on terminated/cli_disconnected — they fire on EVERY relaunch (old proc exit drives SM to terminated; old backend adapter drop broadcasts cli_disconnected). Clear only on terminal frames: session_init (success, also surfaces the fallback-model system message), cli_failed (relaunch-exhausted), session_evicted (archived). fact: Codex model-validation that reads ~/.codex/models_cache.json passes locally but fails CI/fresh-accounts where the cache is absent.
recommendation: Validate-before-kill (resolveCodexLaunchModel) belongs ONLY on the relaunch path where a LIVE process can be stranded. On the initial launch() path there is nothing to strand, so a hard throw when the cache is missing just breaks CI runners and fresh accounts. Make launch() best-effort: upgrade to a launchable slug when the cache is present, otherwise pass the requested model through. In cli-launcher.test.ts, vi.mock('./codex-models.js') with a fixed launchable list so tests exercise control flow, not the host's on-disk cache (the node:fs mock's isMockedPath did NOT route .codex, so it fell through to real fs — the source of local/CI divergence).
